title.narrative: Supporting Safe and Dignified Return in Dar'a, Hrak subdistrict through Integrated WASH, Shelter, and Education Interventions

description.narrative: ltpgtIt responds to the returnees’ and vulnerable host communities’ urgent shelter, education, and WASH in Hrak, Dar’a Governorate, experiencing a steady influx of IDPs and refugee returnees, placing immense pressure on already weakened infrastructure and basic services. It targets 10,425 returnees and vulnerable host community and is designed to restore access to essential services, focusing on sustainable reintegration, protection, and community resilience. ltbrgtSIF is currently intervening in Hrak by repairing 50 damaged houses and supporting vulnerable returnee households to access safe and dignified shelter. The proposed project will complement this ongoing effort, further expanding assistance in Hrak by addressing critical gaps in shelter, education, and WASH services. In the shelter sector, SIF will rehabilitate 120 damaged houses classified into three levels of damage: minor (5) includes doors, windows, plumbing, and electricity moderate (107) includes doors, windows, plumbing, electricity, masonry, and concrete and heavy (8) includes doors, windows, plumbing, electricity, masonry, concrete, and reinforced concrete. Many returnees currently reside in partially damaged houses or share overcrowded spaces with relatives, lacking privacy, protection, and access to basic services. It prioritizes households with heightened vulnerabilities, including returnees, female-headed households, ensuring secure tenure, reduced protection risks, and improved living conditions for approximately 720 PiN. Most targeted HH have valid HLP documentation, enabling legally grounded reconstruction support and facilitating sustainable reintegration.ltbrgtIn Education, SIF will undertake the maintenance of six schools, provide essential furniture, and install solar panels to ensure a safe and conducive learning environment, thereby enhancing school accessibility and safety, particularly for girls and boys at risk of dropping out due to inadequate facilities. In tandem, SIF will implement targeted remedial learning support for 1,100 students, deliver professional development for 80 teachers, and establish 6 PTAs to foster inclusive, community-led initiatives. In addition, bridging activities will be offered for 450 OoSC to support their reintegration into formal education pathways. A health and hygiene promotion component will also be implemented, combining awareness sessions and hygiene kit distribution to 1,400 students to promote safer, healthier school environments. These efforts enhance protective, quality, and inclusive education for returnee and at-risk children, supporting their reintegration and development well-being.ltbrgtIn WASH sector, SIF will restore water access for approximately 8,000 residents, including returnees, by repairing around 1,800 LM of damaged water networks and installing main water valves. This will address critical water scarcity and inequitable distribution, which have forced many to rely on costly water trucking or unsafe sources. By rehabilitating water network and installing main valves and emergency valves, the project will enhance control over water distribution, minimize reverse flow and leakage, and ensure fair and efficient access to drinking water across all neighborhoods. The per capita water share is expected to increase from 30–35 liters to at least 60 liters per day, significantly improving public health, reducing local tensions over access, and strengthening the resilience and sustainability of water services for the entire Hrak community of 42,500 people.ltbrgtSIF will mainstream protection and accountability by delivering PSEA and AAP training for all staff, disseminating key messages to communities, establishing complaint and feedback mechanisms, and ensuring safe referral pathways for individuals at risk. By combining targeted sectoral interventions with community-based approaches, this project supports dignified returns, fosters social cohesion, and enhances resilience in one of Syria’s most underserved return areas.ltbrgtlt/pgt
